input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Sentinel loses its __reduce_ex__, so pickling a member falls back to Enum's default reduction by value, and the value object() cannot be looked up on unpickling
- failure path: pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(UNSET)) rebuilds the member through Enum's default reduction by value; the reconstructed object() matches no Sentinel member, so unpickling raises ValueError; any parameter default holding UNSET that crosses a pickle boundary (multiprocessing, a cache) fails to load

Reviewer finding
- description: Removing the custom __reduce_ex__ breaks pickling of the UNSET and FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE sentinels, because the default Enum reduce reconstructs members by value lookup against the object() values.
- rationale: Trigger: pickling a value that holds Sentinel.UNSET, such as an option or context default, then unpickling it. Mechanism: the default Enum __reduce_ex__ serializes the member's object() value, and on load Sentinel(value) compares by equality against the original object(), which fails because the unpickled object is a new instance, raising ValueError. Impact: unpickling fails or the sentinel identity is lost, so 'is UNSET' checks stop matching after a pickle round trip.
critique: The finding names the same cause as the label: the custom __reduce_ex__ was removed, so Enum falls back to its default reduce by value. It also gives the same failure, where the unpickled object() matches no member and Sentinel(value) raises ValueError when loading.
